clue.text: Accumulation of electricity in storm

definitions.meaning: an electrical build-up held on a body, as on a battery or a cloud
to storm a position is to rush at it in an attack

explanation.surface: A thundercloud builds up static during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to one word: the electric quantity stored on a body, and a headlong attack or rush, which is what storming means.

clue.text: Enclose a division of the celestial sphere

definitions.meaning: to enclose something is to give it shelter or a home

definitions.text: a division of the celestial sphere
definitions.meaning: astrologers split the sky into twelve sectors, each ruling part of life

explanation.surface: An astronomer fences off one sector of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to shelter or contain; in astrology it names one of the twelve sectors the heavens are divided into.

clue.text: Mineral needed in arboreal gardens

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words arboreal gardens

explanation.surface: A gardener says a certain mineral is required in tree-filled gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'arboreal' and runs into 'gardens'.
explanation.definitionFit: Realgar is an orange-red arsenic sulphide ore, a mineral once used as a pigment.

clue.text: Battery parts with old copper in steel core, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the old coin inside the rearranged letters
perhaps signals that the letters of steel core are to be taken in some other order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A battery has terminals made using an ancient copper coin set in a steel core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges STEEL CORE into ELECTROES, and 'in' puts D inside it. The old penny, written d, was a copper coin before decimal currency came in in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrodes are the terminals through which current enters or leaves a battery cell.

clue.text: Apparent difference in position, standard with a line showing latitude

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
latitude as freedom from strictness is laxity, so lax

explanation.surface: A navigator draws a standard line to show latitude on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' looks geographical but means leeway, giving LAX.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy and optics the term names the shift an object seems to make when seen from two different viewpoints.

clue.text: What may come from oil, say, that'll be released in fall

definitions.text: What may come from oil, say, that'll be released in fall

parts.words: What may come from oil, say, that'll be released in fall
parts.note: stored power, such as that locked in fuel or in a raised weight, which is set free when the body drops

explanation.surface: A riddle about something got from oil that is set free when a thing drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics names the energy a body holds by position or chemistry, as in a raised weight or a fuel, which is turned into motion when it falls.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance from subjects in lab experiments

definitions.meaning: an exclamation like drat or damn
rodents commonly used for testing in laboratories

explanation.surface: A scientist curses at the animals being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural rodent name doubles as a mild curse of irritation, and these animals are standard laboratory test subjects.

clue.text: Article found in vessel, book in ancient script

indicators.note: found in places the article inside the word for a vessel

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds an item in a pot and a book written in an old script.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear B is the Mycenaean Greek syllabic writing found on Bronze Age clay tablets.

clue.text: Gravity causes collapse, trapping a number

indicators.note: trapping means the number is held inside the rearranged letters
to collapse is to fall apart, so the letters of causes are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Gravity makes something cave in, catching a number inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' turns CAUSES into ACUESS, and 'trapping' holds TEN inside it after ACU. 'Gravity' looks like physics, but it means seriousness; the acute and grave accents add a wink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity in the sense of severity or seriousness of a situation is matched by its sharpness or intensity.

clue.text: Apart from neon, including a natural gas

indicators.note: including means the letter a is held within the other letters

parts.note: but means except or apart from
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: A chemist describes a natural gas, with neon set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts A into BUT + NE, between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Butane is a hydrocarbon found in and extracted from natural gas deposits.

clue.text: Metal — cast it in less than a minute, perhaps

indicators.note: cast, as metal is shaped in a mould, tells us to form the letters into a new shape
less than means a little is short, so the final letter of the phrase a minute is dropped

explanation.surface: A foundry worker boasts of casting a piece of metal in under sixty seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' cuts the E from A MINUTE to leave AMINUT; with IT those letters are 'cast' into the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong, light, silvery transition metal.

clue.text: Crew put in helium and nitrogen to increase altitude

indicators.note: put in means the crew goes inside the pair of element symbols

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A balloon crew pumps in gases so the craft can climb higher.
explanation.walkthrough: EIGHT, a rowing crew, goes between HE and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or make taller is to add altitude, a sense matched by making something higher.

clue.text: Scientific device-one not working well, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: someone lazing about, a lazer, is not working hard

explanation.surface: A broken lab instrument is said to be idle.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lazer', one who lazes, is pronounced the same as the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is an optical instrument emitting a narrow, intense beam of coherent light.

clue.text: What's the matter, fundamentally, in 10 or 16, say

definitions.text: What's the matter, fundamentally, in 10 or 16, say

parts.words: What's the matter, fundamentally, in 10 or 16, say
parts.note: the amount of matter in one basic unit of an element such as the metals at 10 and 16

explanation.surface: A worried question about what is wrong with two other entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the matter' sounds like concern but asks how much matter, at the level of atoms, the metals TITANIUM (10) and THORIUM (16) have.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure gives the weight of one atom of an element, the matter at its fundamental level.

clue.text: He comes second here, and I can be found in fifty-third place

definitions.text: He comes second here, and I can be found in fifty-third place

parts.words: He comes second here, and I can be found in fifty-third place
parts.note: He and I are the chemical symbols of helium and iodine, numbers two and fifty-three in the chart of the chemical elements

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that a man finished second and the speaker came fifty-third in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' and 'I' read as pronouns, but they are element symbols: helium has atomic number 2 and iodine 53.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart arranges the chemical elements by atomic number, so helium is second and iodine fifty-third.

clue.text: Corruptly reproduce part of computer program

indicators.note: corruptly suggests the letters of reproduce are garbled out of their order

explanation.surface: Copying a section of software dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: In programming, a subroutine or self-contained block of instructions is called by this name.

clue.text: See 14
Unusually hot alcoholic spirit in which one's plunged metal

indicators.note: unusually shows the letters of hot are set out in an odd order
one plunged into the drink is put inside the word for that spirit

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit
one is I, the Roman numeral, the 's being linking

explanation.surface: An oddly hot rum into which someone dunks a piece of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' turns HOT into THO; I, one, goes into RUM, with 'in which' only joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorium is a radioactive metallic element of the actinide series.

clue.text: Runs messy vote somehow — that's how brainwaves get to the members

definitions.text: that's how brainwaves get to the members

indicators.note: somehow shows the letters of the phrase are put into an order not yet known

explanation.surface: A chaotic ballot is being run, and that is how ideas reach the party members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests club or party members, but means limbs, which the brain's signals reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's network of nerves carries the brain's signals to the limbs.

clue.text: Elementary particle featured in theme song

indicators.note: featured in means the answer appears inside the run of letters across theme song

explanation.surface: A tiny particle gets a mention in a show's theme tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A meson is a subatomic particle made of a quark and an antiquark.

clue.text: Alloy chemist, in short, mixed with iron

indicators.note: mixed shows the letters are stirred together into a new order
in short means the word chemist is cut down to a shorter form

explanation.surface: A chemist briefly blends iron to make an alloy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' cuts CHEMIST to CHEM; 'mixed' shuffles CHEM with IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Nichrome is a nickel-chromium alloy used for heating elements.

clue.text: Optical equipment I use? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: the speaker's own organ of sight
an exclamation of disbelief, like rubbish or tosh

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of the speaker using optical gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase is the speaker's organ of sight; as an exclamation it means 'rubbish!', expressing disbelief.

clue.text: Gold is layered thinly, primarily, for this

definitions.text: Gold is layered thinly, primarily, for this

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the words gold is layered thinly

explanation.surface: Gold is beaten into thin layers mainly for this purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a thin coat of gold applied to a surface.

clue.text: One can decontaminate Indian port with fire, perhaps

parts.note: Puri is a coastal city in Odisha, eastern India

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of fire may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An Indian port might be cleansed by fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or agent that removes contamination cleans, so it is named for making things pure.

clue.text: A page with curve showing extreme position in orbit

parts.note: an ogee is an S-shaped curve or moulding

explanation.surface: A diagram on a page uses a curve to show the far point of an orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apogee is the point in an orbit furthest from the Earth.

clue.text: With George and me, experiment in study of space

parts.note: Geo is a short form of the name George
a try is an attempt or experiment

explanation.surface: George and the speaker run an experiment on space.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with shapes, sizes and spatial relations.

clue.text: See 17
